question: What do you manufacture, in which locations, and at what approximate annual volume?
Who are your main customers and markets (e.g., automotive, food, consumer goods, construction)?
What are your top 3 business priorities over the next 3-5 years (growth, cost reduction, quality, innovation, etc.)?
What is your long term sustainability ambition (e.g., compliance only, industry leader, net-zero, circular products)?
Are you aiming for any certifications or frameworks (ISO 14001, ISO 50001, B Corp, Science Based Targets, GRI reporting, etc.)?
Do you currently measure energy use, water consumption, waste, and emissions (e.g., electricity, gas, water, waste to landfill, recycling rates)?
Do you know your main “hotspots” of environmental impact (e.g., raw materials, specific processes, packaging, transport, product use phase)?
Have you conducted a carbon footprint, life cycle assessment, or environmental audit of your operations or products?
What environmental regulations already apply to your sites (air, water, waste, chemicals, extended producer responsibility)?
Are there any recurring environmental incidents or complaints (e.g., spills, noise, odors, waste issues, community concerns)?
What are your main production processes, and which ones consume the most energy and water?
Which fuels and energy sources do you use (grid electricity, natural gas, diesel, LPG, renewables on-site)?
How is waste currently managed (recycling, landfill, incineration, hazardous waste), and do you know approximate quantities or costs?
What are your main raw materials and packaging types, and how recyclable, renewable, or hazardous are they?
Do you already have any efficiency or lean programs (e.g., energy-saving projects, scrap reduction, OEE improvement, TPM/lean initiatives)?
How long do your products typically last, and what happens to them at end-of-life (reused, recycled, landfilled)?
Do you have influence over product design (materials choice, modular design, reparability, recyclability)?
Are you exploring circular models (take-back schemes, remanufacturing, refurbishing, product-as-a-service, reuse of by-products)?
Do customers ask for environmental data (product carbon footprint, recycled content, eco-labels, EPDs)?
Where do your critical raw materials and components come from (regions, key suppliers)?
Do you have a supplier code of conduct or sustainability requirements for suppliers?
Are you collecting any data from suppliers (e.g., emissions, energy, certifications, social practices)?
How are inbound and outbound logistics organized (modes of transport, typical distances, frequency of shipments)?
Are there risks related to materials scarcity, conflict minerals, deforestation, or volatile prices?
Who currently “owns” sustainability in your organization (if anyone), and how much decision-making power do they have?
How aware and engaged are employees on environmental and social topics?
What are your main health, safety, and labor priorities (accident reduction, ergonomics, training, diversity and inclusion)?
Do you have any existing social or community initiatives (local hiring, apprenticeships, philanthropy, volunteering)?
How does leadership currently talk about sustainability (risk avoidance, cost saving, brand differentiation, innovation)?
Do you already have any quantified sustainability targets (e.g., energy per unit, waste reduction %, CO₂ reduction, water use, incident rates)?
What time horizon for targets is realistic for you (1-2 years, 3-5 years, 10+ years)?
Which metrics would be most meaningful for your business (per unit produced, per revenue, site‑level totals, etc.)?
How often can you realistically collect and review data (monthly, quarterly, annually)?
Do your key customers or investors require ESG or sustainability reporting, and in what format?
What level of annual budget could you allocate to sustainability initiatives in the next 1-3 years?
What payback periods are acceptable for investments (e.g., <2 years, 3-5 years, longer if strategic)?
What operational constraints do you face (limited downtime, legacy equipment, space constraints, skills gaps)?
Where do you see the biggest business opportunities from sustainability (new markets, premium pricing, better customer retention, cost savings)?
Which climate or environment-related risks could affect your operations (flooding, heat, supply disruption, energy price volatility, regulation)?
Are you required or likely to be required soon to report on climate or sustainability risks (e.g., by large customers, banks, or regulations)?
How resilient are your supply chains to geopolitical issues, climate impacts, and regulatory changes?
Who are the internal champions that could lead or sponsor sustainability efforts?
How do you usually manage cross-functional projects (governance structure, KPIs, review cadence)?
What training or capability building would your teams need to deliver the plan?
How would you like to communicate progress internally (dashboards, town halls, suggestion schemes) and externally (website, reports, customer updates)?
